summary: This work demonstrates sympathetic cooling of trapped $^{43}$Ca$^+$ ions using same-species and same-isotope ions, with both data and coolant qubits encoded in the ground-state $4S_{1/2}$ manifold and addressed via microwave-driven pulsed sideband cooling. The scheme achieves ground-state cooling of a two-ion rocking mode to $\bar{n} \approx 0.16$ phonons with an induced error of $1.7(4) \times 10^{-4}$ per cooling cycle on the data qubit.
motivation: Conventional sympathetic cooling uses a second ion species to avoid crosstalk, requiring additional laser infrastructure and complicating optical setups. Implementing same-isotope cooling with microwave control simplifies the experiment while enabling quantum-information preservation in clock-state qubits within the ground manifold.
method: Data and coolant ions are separated in frequency using Zeeman splitting in a static magnetic field of 28.8 mT. Pulsed resolved-sideband cooling drives the $|3,2\rangle \to |4,2\rangle$ motional sideband at 2.908 GHz with compensation tones to cancel ac Zeeman shifts; cooling cycles are interleaved with spin-echo pulses on the data qubit ($|4,1\rangle$ to $|3,1\rangle$ at 3.123 GHz) to correct residual frequency drifts.
result: After 16 cooling cycles, the in-plane radial rocking mode ($\omega = 2\pi \times 5.37$ MHz) is cooled from $1.7(2)$ quanta to $\bar{n} = 0.16(2)$ quanta at a rate of $0.27(1)$ quanta/cycle; the data qubit error is dominated by thermal drifts in the microwave drive chain at $1.2(3) \times 10^{-4}$ per cycle from the sideband pulse, with a fundamental limit from 393 nm photon scattering estimated at $1.6(9) \times 10^{-6}$ per cycle.
